Alice Chen: Ok team — quarterly planning sync: need a concrete proposal for SOC2 launch criteria + audit-evidence playbook by EOD Fri. Customers pushing on per-tenant retention & HSM proofs.
Marco Rivera: +1. Can we scope a minimal path that satisfies auditors without overbuilding HSM for v1?
Priya Nair: We should split requirements: 1) audit log schema & retention, 2) keystore (KMS vs HSM) requirements, 3) evidence export & legal hold. Each with launch criteria.
Jordan Lee: For KMS vs HSM: engineering effort differs a lot. KMS integration + KMS CMEK is quick. HSM (FIPS 140-2/3) needs procurement + infra + attestation. Timeline = months.
Samir Patel: From sales: three enterprise prospects explicitly require HSM-backed key material and deterministic rotation logs. They might sign if we can show roadmap milestone + temporary compensating control.
Alice Chen: Ok — draft suggestion: v1 (SOC2 readiness milestone): KMS with immutable audit logs, per-tenant rotation metadata, exportable evidence bundle. v2: optional HSM-backed keys + signing of log digests. Thoughts?
Marco Rivera: That could work. Need to define "immutable audit logs" — do we use append-only storage + signed digests? We can implement log signing with KMS asymmetric keys to reduce HSM need initially.
Priya Nair: Agree. Launch criteria for v1 could be: 1) audit logs capture: request id, user id, model id, route, token usage, KMS key id, rotation events. 2) 90-day retention default, configurable per-tenant up to N days. 3) Exportable evidence bundle (JSONL + signature). 4) SOC2: internal controls documented and automated sampling.
Jordan Lee: Quick note: 90-day default might upset legal — we need legal hold option to preserve data beyond retention. Also need deletion proof for customers who request deletion.
Samir Patel: Sales asks for per-tenant retention policy UI and API. Also want legal hold API: `POST /tenants/:id/legal_hold` -> prevents deletion.
Marco Rivera: API surface is fine. Engineering estimate for v1 (KMS + log signing + export): 4-6 sprints for eng-runtime + infra + console. Add 2 sprints for QA & SOC2 evidence collection.
Priya Nair: Can we reduce scope by shipping audit export first as a beta (no UI) for customers who need evidence quickly? That would be smaller: store logs, provide `GET /evidence/:bundle` endpoint.
Alice Chen: Good idea — beta export could be launchable earlier. Launch criteria should be explicit: - logs ingested >= 99% reliability for production routes, - export contains signed manifests, - docs + runbook for auditors.
Jordan Lee: Need to call out log schema. Proposal snippet:
```
{
  "ts": "...",
  "request_id": "...",
  "actor": "user@example.com",
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "model": "redwood/llama-13b-v1",
  "route": "generate",
  "tokens_in": 12,
  "tokens_out": 200,
  "kms_key_id": "projects/.../locations/.../keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/k",
  "event_type": "rotate_key|delete_key|grant_role",
  "signature": "base64sig"
}
```
Priya Nair: Schema looks good. Add `retention_exempt` flag for legal_hold + `exported_at` timestamp.
Samir Patel: Also add `redaction_marker` for PII redaction events so we can show deletion proofs.
Alice Chen: Good. On HSM: for v2 we should support HSM-backed KEKs and also provide attestation docs. We can offer an "HSM on ramp" with contractual SLA and migration runbook.
Marco Rivera: Implementation note: using KMS asymmetric signing for logs means customers can get signed evidence without us needing HSM immediately. For customers that require HSM, we can route sign operations to HSM-backed keys in later release.
Jordan Lee: Cost tradeoffs: signing every log adds CPU; better to sign periodic digests (e.g., hourly merkle root). That reduces cost and still provides tamper-evidence.
Priya Nair: Agreed. Let's specify digest cadence: default hourly; configurable to daily for low-volume tenants, real-time for high-security customers (extra cost).
Samir Patel: Sales: price premium for per-tenant HSM + real-time signing. Need rough pricing model for proposals.
Alice Chen: Action items: Marco/ Jordan write tech spec for v1 KMS + digest signing by Wed. Priya draft SOC2 controls mapping + evidence checklist. Samir draft customer-facing messaging and pricing guidelines. I'll own the launch criteria doc and timeline.
security-bot: Reminder: RFC template available at https://redwood-internal/rfc. Please attach spec to RFC-SEC-2026-02.
Marco Rivera: Quick Q — retention default = 90 days but what about embeddings & vector cache? Those are sensitive and often excluded from audit logs. We need to cover embedding storage separately.
Priya Nair: Good catch. Add requirement: embedding vectors should be deletable on tenant request and flagged in evidence bundle if retained.
Jordan Lee: Timeline sync: if we start Monday, 4-6 sprints estimate means v1 beta export could be available by end of Q2. HSM target Q4.
Samir Patel: I'll align with three customers and see if beta meets their needs (legal teams usually accept signed export while HSM is in roadmap).
Alice Chen: Ok — let's keep the plan lean. We want SOC2 readiness for internal audit by end of Q2; production-grade enterprise HSM by Q4. Document everything in the RFC and link to product roadmap item.
Marco Rivera: I'll drop an initial RFC link when done. Any blockers?
Priya Nair: Need legal to confirm retention bounds and regulatory minimums for EU customers. I'll ping legal.
Samir Patel: I'll collect customer acceptance criteria and share sample contract language.
Alice Chen: Thanks everyone — sync again Thursday 9am to review drafts. :thumbsup:
Marco Rivera: :thumbsup:
Priya Nair: ack
Jordan Lee: ack
Samir Patel: ack
